correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=5, use the concave Rayleigh variational expression to average any feasible edge assignment over price-preserving automorphisms. Exact Fourier/layer-parity diagonalization gives the full spectrum sigma_k(a+c) and sigma_k a+(4-sigma_k)c+2b; the spectral gap is the minimum of mu(a+c),4c+2b,beta a+delta c+2b. The cost-minimization polyhedron for gap>=1 has only four feasible vertices for even n and five for odd n: the all-positive three-plane intersection requires b=(1-2U)/2<0, while separate zero-coordinate sections give the listed points. A positive homogeneous rescaling therefore yields 1/(n J_min), and every invariant minimizer is a convex combination of the minimum-cost vertices. Price thresholds arise by explicit affine-cost comparison. The independent checker ran successfully: 45 vertex matches, 850 price comparisons, 130 direct full spectra, 430 irregular budget cases, 640 phase checks. All experiments are finite and supplemental; the analytic proof covers arbitrary n and positive prices.

originality.rationale: The principal specialization is an exact three-independent-price maximization of the continuous-time second Laplacian eigenvalue on the strong circular prism, with a parity-sensitive four/five-vertex optimum and full orbit-symmetric optimizer face. The general SDP formulation, unweighted strong-product spectral decomposition, resistance/spanning-tree tables and multilayer interlink-only optimization do not supply or logically entail this exact price classification without additional analysis. Search results revealed no matching published theorem; this is supportive but not absolute novelty proof. Residual risks are recorded.
residual_risks: Historical specialized exact spectral optimization for crossed cyclic ladders could exist under other terminology or in an unindexed source.
The unit-weight block spectral proof in Pan and Li readily motivates, but does not itself prove, the independently priced optimality classification.
Generality of the Sun et al. convex program should not be confused with an explicit solution for this graph.
Only class-symmetric optimal designs are classified; possible further nonsymmetric equality cases are outside the claim.
The finite checker is supportive, not an independent proof or independent external audit.

value.rationale: The question is a natural resource-allocation design problem in a two-layer ring with three distinct connection types. Four or five exact class-symmetric unit-gap designs exhaust all possible price optima, producing a sharp explicit three-parameter phase diagram for arbitrary order. The odd/even topology leads to a meaningful qualitative design distinction: crossed diagonals alone become a connected optimizer only for odd n, with a calculable cost threshold and nontrivial degenerate tie faces. These are structural global design facts, not merely numerical table recomputations; the precise invariant and price model are motivated by mixing and resource tradeoffs. No broader graph-product theorem is asserted.
